new_hypotheses: Explicit working-pointer copies and early scale temporaries: no codegen change.
Unsigned input ID matches retail cmplwi.
Initializing special immediately after the target lookup and before its predicate reproduces the retail call-spanning Boolean live range.

Const qualification of the scale (config/GEDE01/symbols.txt identifies lbl_806510D0 as a float in .sdata2) permits early load scheduling and reserves f1, producing retail f4 conversion bias. This is the main new hypothesis and gain.

Initializer order, scalar versus aggregate locals, parameter reuse, and midpoint evaluation structure were measured under the new control-flow and const-qualified form. Declaration permutations with separated initialization generally generated identical code.

The low-word extraction was evaluated only after the new const-qualified schedule and predicate form; in this combination it reproduces the missing li/and pair and exact 728-byte size. The old mask-only regression was not retained.
retained_changes: separate handle/item/kind initialization in retail order
special initialized after target lookup with no else assignment
separate midpoint component loads and sums followed by signed shifts
probe_notes: All probes used the existing canonical compiler command and flags.

Probe literals were validated with tools/externalize_elf_symbol.py --require-whole-section and renamed using the existing rule operations before strict comparison. The selected literal is @48; configure.py changes only this target rule literal spelling.

The initial special and comma-expression probes changed the generated literal name, so the old @49 rule rejected them. They were remeasured after resolving the actual literal and applying the existing guarded externalization.
A variable aggregate initializer was rejected by canonical C mode as an illegal constant expression; it was not retained.
